decks.domain: Young drivers, permits, license classes, renewals, ID cards and fees

cards.front: What must an applicant under eighteen provide besides a co-signing parent or guardian?
cards.back: An applicant under eighteen for a license, DAC or instruction permit needs a parent or guardian to co-sign and must sign an affidavit acknowledging the penalties that apply to young drivers.

cards.front: What alcohol reading costs a young driver a revocation, and for how long?
cards.back: A young driver's license can be revoked for one hundred eighty-five days when a blood, breath or urine test shows an alcohol level of at least zero point zero two percent but less than zero point zero eight percent by weight.

cards.front: What does any court finding that a young driver drove impaired bring?
cards.back: Any court finding that a young driver drove under the influence of alcohol or a controlled substance also brings a one hundred eighty-five-day revocation.

cards.front: Which offenses can suspend or delay a young driver's license for up to two years?
cards.back: Graffiti or defacing property, crimes tied to alcohol or a controlled substance, any use, possession, sale or distribution of a controlled substance, or buying, drinking or possessing alcohol can each mean suspension or delayed issuance for up to two years.

cards.front: What penalty follows a firearm offense under the young-driver rules?
cards.back: Handling or possessing a firearm in violation of NRS two hundred two point three zero zero means suspension or delayed issuance for up to one year, and two years for a second offense.

cards.front: What penalties apply for a first and a repeat habitual-truancy offense?
cards.back: A first habitual-truancy offense brings a suspension of thirty days to six months or a thirty-day delay; a second or later offense brings sixty days to one year or a sixty-day delay (NRS three hundred ninety-two point one four eight).

cards.front: What penalty follows a conviction for a speed contest or trick driving display?
cards.back: A conviction for joining or organizing an unauthorized speed contest, or for driving in or facilitating an unauthorized trick driving display, brings a suspension of six months to two years.

cards.front: What penalties does a young first-time DUI offender face?
cards.back: A young driver who becomes a first-time DUI offender faces the same penalties as a driver over twenty-one.

cards.front: How does a low alcohol reading for a young driver differ from a first DUI offense?
cards.back: A low alcohol reading between zero point zero two percent and zero point zero eight percent already costs a young driver a one hundred eighty-five-day revocation, while a first DUI offense puts the young driver under the full adult penalties.

decks.domain: Young drivers, permits, license classes, renewals, ID cards and fees

cards.front: What two documents must a teen bring for a license or DAC drive test?
cards.back: A teen applying for a license or DAC must present a driver's education Certificate of Completion and the Beginning Driver Experience Log (DMV Form DLD-one hundred thirty), filled in with blue or black ink before arriving for the drive test.

cards.front: What attendance form must a permit applicant under eighteen give the DMV?
cards.back: Anyone under eighteen applying for an instruction permit must give the DMV a DMV-three hundred one Certification of Attendance signed by the principal or a designated school official confirming minimum attendance.

cards.front: What does a minor who has finished school submit with the attendance form?
cards.back: A minor who has finished school submits the DMV-three hundred one with a copy of a high school diploma or an equivalency (GED, HiSET or TASC), and the form must be signed and dated within the previous sixty days.

cards.front: What must a former habitual truant bring before driving privileges are reinstated?
cards.back: A student previously declared a habitual truant under NRS three hundred ninety-two point one four four whose license or permit was suspended must bring a new DMV-three hundred one showing current attendance before driving privileges are reinstated.

cards.front: Where can driver's education be completed?
cards.back: Driver's education can be completed at a local DMV-approved school or online through a DMV-approved school.

cards.front: Who may log one hundred behind-the-wheel hours instead of taking driver's education?
cards.back: Only a teen living more than thirty miles from an approved school who cannot take an online class may instead log one hundred hours of behind-the-wheel driving, ten of them in the dark.

cards.front: How many supervised hours must a teen near an approved school complete?
cards.back: Teens within thirty miles of an approved driver's education school must complete fifty hours of supervised driving, ten of them at night, recorded on the official DMV form.

cards.front: How do the standard and remote practice-hour paths compare?
cards.back: The standard path is fifty supervised hours with ten at night; the remote path for teens beyond thirty miles of a school and without internet access is one hundred hours with ten in the dark.

cards.front: What extra rule applies to remote-path practice hours for a motorcycle license?
cards.back: For a motorcycle license on the remote path, all one hundred practice hours must be driven in daylight only.

cards.front: What must a minor's record show for six months before licensing?
cards.back: A minor must go six months without an at-fault crash, a moving violation conviction or any alcohol or drug conviction before receiving a license.

decks.domain: Young drivers, permits, license classes, renewals, ID cards and fees

cards.front: How long is a Nevada instruction permit valid, and when must it be carried?
cards.back: A Nevada instruction permit is valid for one year and must be carried whenever the holder drives.

cards.front: What do you need to get a Nevada instruction permit?
cards.back: To get a permit you must be at least fifteen and a half, complete an application, pass a vision test and a knowledge test on traffic laws, signs, markings and safe driving, and have a parent or guardian available to authorize it.

cards.front: Who may supervise a Class C permit holder, and where must that person sit?
cards.back: A Class C permit holder may drive only with a licensed driver who is twenty-one or older, has at least one year of licensed experience and sits in the seat beside the permit holder.

cards.front: How long must an applicant under eighteen hold a permit before applying for a license?
cards.back: Applicants under eighteen must hold an instruction permit for at least six months before applying for a license.

cards.front: What passenger limit applies to new sixteen- and seventeen-year-old licensees?
cards.back: For their first six months of driving, new licensees who were sixteen or seventeen at issuance may not carry passengers under eighteen except immediate family members (NRS four hundred eighty-three point two five two three).

cards.front: When may a minor not drive, and how long does that curfew last?
cards.back: A minor may not drive between ten p.m. and five a.m. unless driving to or from a scheduled event, and this curfew lasts until the driver turns eighteen regardless of when the license was issued.

cards.front: How does supervision differ for a Class C permit and a motorcycle permit?
cards.back: A Class C permit supervisor sits in the seat beside you, while a motorcycle or moped permit supervisor must ride a motorcycle within direct sight and may not be in a car or truck.

cards.front: What limits apply to a motorcycle or moped permit holder?
cards.back: A Class M or M-Z permit holder rides in daylight only, carries no passengers and stays off limited-access highways and freeways.

cards.front: What are the three six-month rules for Nevada teens?
cards.back: Three different six-month rules apply to Nevada teens: hold the permit at least six months, carry no non-family passengers under eighteen for the first six months of licensed driving, and stay crash- and conviction-free for six months before licensing.

decks.domain: Young drivers, permits, license classes, renewals, ID cards and fees

cards.front: Which tests does every license class require?
cards.back: Every license class requires vision and knowledge tests, and a road test in the type of vehicle to be driven may also be required.

cards.front: What must a Class C holder pass to ride a motorcycle?
cards.back: A Class C holder who also wants to ride a motorcycle must pass a written test on motorcycle laws and practices and a motorcycle drive test.

cards.front: What license lets you ride a moped?
cards.back: Any Nevada driver license class lets you ride a moped, or you can apply for a Class M license restricted to mopeds only.

cards.front: What vehicles does Class C cover, and what may it tow?
cards.back: Class C covers cars, vans and pickups and may tow a vehicle of ten thousand pounds or less, and any combination of vehicles may not exceed seventy feet.

cards.front: What do the common restriction codes on a Nevada license mean?
cards.back: Common restriction codes are B for glasses or contacts, F for added rearview mirrors, G for daylight driving only, six for a yearly vision exam, seven for a yearly medical letter, eight for a yearly driving test and JN for instruction permit.

cards.front: What do Classes A, B and M cover?
cards.back: Class A covers combinations rated over twenty-six thousand pounds GCWR with a trailer over ten thousand pounds, Class B covers a single vehicle over twenty-six thousand pounds GVWR that may tow under ten thousand pounds, and Class M covers motorcycles and mopeds.
cards.memory_hook: A combos, B heavy, M bikes

cards.front: Where are the extra tests for commercial drivers described?
cards.back: Commercial drivers must pass additional knowledge and skills tests described in the separate Commercial Driver's License Handbook.

cards.front: What is an endorsement, and what does each one require?
cards.back: An endorsement allows driving a vehicle that needs more skill than a typical vehicle, and each one needs additional tests.

cards.front: What does the J endorsement allow a Class C driver to tow, and within what limits?
cards.back: The J endorsement lets a Class C driver tow a vehicle or combination rated above ten thousand pounds, provided the combination stays within seventy feet and twenty-six thousand pounds; above twenty-six thousand pounds a Class A license is required.

cards.front: Who is covered by the F endorsement exemption?
cards.back: The F endorsement is a commercial-license exemption for firefighters operating fire equipment, for military members driving military vehicles on active duty, and for farm employees or family hauling supplies within one hundred fifty miles of the farm unless they are a common or contract carrier or carry placarded hazardous materials.

cards.front: What makes a vehicle a commercial motor vehicle?
cards.back: A commercial motor vehicle is one used in commerce with a weight rating of twenty-six thousand one pounds or more, or designed for sixteen or more people including the driver, or carrying hazardous materials.

cards.front: How long does a motorcycle permit last at different ages?
cards.back: A motorcycle permit issued between fifteen and a half and eighteen lasts one year, but one issued after age seventeen expires on the eighteenth birthday; at eighteen or older it lasts six months and can be renewed only once every five years.

cards.front: What can replace the motorcycle tests, and what permanently bars a motorcycle permit?
cards.back: Passing an approved motorcycle safety course may replace the motorcycle tests, but failing the DMV motorcycle skills test two or more times permanently bars future motorcycle permits (NRS four hundred eighty-three point two eight zero).

cards.front: What does a motorcycle license require?
cards.back: A motorcycle license requires age sixteen, a vision test, the general and motorcycle knowledge tests and the Motorcycle Operators Skills Test, and riders must wear a helmet.

decks.domain: Young drivers, permits, license classes, renewals, ID cards and fees

cards.front: Whose job is it to renew a license on time?
cards.back: The expiration date is printed on the front of the license, and renewing on or before it is the driver's responsibility even though a renewal notice is mailed.

cards.front: What tests may be required at renewal?
cards.back: Renewal may call for vision, knowledge and on-road driving tests to re-evaluate the driver and decide on restrictions.

cards.front: How does Nevada handle license renewal for active-duty members out of state?
cards.back: Nevada does not automatically extend licenses for military personnel, but active-duty members temporarily out of state may renew by mail.

cards.front: How soon must you report a change of address or name to the DMV?
cards.back: Nevada law requires you to report any change of address or name to the DMV within thirty days.

cards.front: How can you change your address or name with the DMV?
cards.back: Addresses can be changed online, at a DMV office or by mail with form DMV-twenty-two, but CDL holders must do it in person; name changes are always made in person with legal proof of the new name.

cards.front: Who may receive a restricted license?
cards.back: Restricted licenses may go to drivers aged fourteen and fifteen who show family hardship or need to drive to and from school, and to people who have served half of a suspension or revocation.

cards.front: How does a restricted license differ from the usual path?
cards.back: A restricted license is a special-circumstance exception: drivers of fourteen or fifteen qualify only with family hardship or a school-travel need, and others only after serving half of a suspension or revocation.

cards.front: What should you do with a lost, stolen or illegible license?
cards.back: A lost, stolen or illegible license should be replaced immediately with a duplicate, online or in person, and the DMV may use the record and photo already on file.

decks.domain: Young drivers, permits, license classes, renewals, ID cards and fees

cards.front: What is the minimum age and term for a Nevada ID card?
cards.back: A Nevada ID card requires age ten or older and lasts eight years, expiring on the birthday unless limited-term immigration documents were used.

cards.front: What does being issued a Nevada ID card surrender?
cards.back: Being issued an ID card automatically surrenders your driving privilege and any ID card from Nevada or another state, whether or not you have it with you; seasonal resident ID applicants are the exception.

cards.front: How do traffic citations affect an ID card holder?
cards.back: Traffic citations issued to an ID card holder count against future driving privileges, and twelve or more demerits in twelve months means the privilege must be reinstated before a license can be issued.

cards.front: When does an ID card based on limited-term documents expire?
cards.back: An ID card based on limited-term immigration documents expires on the departure date, or one year after issuance when no date is listed.

cards.front: How can a veteran add a veteran designation?
cards.back: An honorably discharged veteran can add a veteran designation at an initial or renewal license or ID by bringing proof of honorable discharge and signing a release to the Nevada Department of Veterans Services.

cards.front: What does an optional medical indicator require?
cards.back: An optional medical indicator, shown as a recognized medical symbol on the front of the card, needs a completed Confidential Physician Report (DMV Form DLD-seven) naming one listed medical code.

cards.front: When can Organ Donor be added, and what does a minor's parent sign?
cards.back: Organ Donor can be added to a license or ID card at original issuance, renewal or an address change, and a minor's parent or guardian signs an affidavit on the DMV-two accepting that they cannot amend or revoke the donation.

cards.front: What do the donation funds collected by the DMV support?
cards.back: The DMV takes contributions for the Anatomical Gift Account during licensing and through Organ Donor license plates, and gifts of one dollar or more to the Gift of Life Education Fund go to the University of Nevada School of Medicine.

cards.front: What are possible signs of sex trafficking, and what should you never do?
cards.back: Possible signs of sex trafficking include not knowing one's whereabouts, not holding one's own ID or passport, controlled communication and a fearful or submissive manner, and a suspected trafficker should never be confronted.

cards.front: What do an original license and an instruction permit cost under age sixty-five?
cards.back: Fees are set by Nevada state law and can change; under age sixty-five an original license costs forty-one dollars and twenty-five cents and an instruction permit twenty-two dollars and twenty-five cents.

cards.front: What does reinstatement cost after an alcohol offense compared with other offenses?
cards.back: Reinstatement after an alcohol or controlled-substance offense costs one hundred twenty dollars plus a thirty-five dollars victim's fee, while reinstatement for any other offense costs seventy-five dollars.

cards.front: Which fees must be paid after a suspension, revocation or cancellation?
cards.back: Any suspension, revocation or cancellation requires paying the reinstatement fee, the original-license fee and any testing fees that apply.

cards.front: What do drivers sixty-five and older and young ID card applicants pay?
cards.back: Drivers sixty-five and older pay seventeen dollars and twenty-five cents for an original, duplicate, renewal or instruction permit, and ID cards for ages ten to seventeen cost nine dollars and twenty-five cents.

cards.front: What do an address change and a retest cost?
cards.back: A change of address alone costs three dollars and twenty-five cents, and each knowledge and skills retest costs ten dollars after the twenty-five dollars initial test fee.

cards.front: What extra fee does reinstating a commercial license require?
cards.back: Reinstating a commercial license also requires paying a non-CDL reinstatement fee.

recap_hooks.text: A young driver with a low alcohol reading loses the license for one hundred eighty-five days, and a first DUI brings the adult penalties.
Drug, alcohol, graffiti, firearm, truancy and street-racing offenses can each suspend or delay a young driver's license.
Permit applicants under eighteen bring a signed school attendance form.
Teens near an approved school log fifty supervised hours with ten at night; remote teens log one hundred.
Six months without an at-fault crash or conviction comes before a minor's license.
A permit lasts one year, and a Class C supervisor is twenty-one or older with a year of experience, seated beside you.
Teens hold the permit six months, carry only family passengers under eighteen for six months, and stay off the road from ten at night to five in the morning until eighteen.
Class C covers cars, vans and pickups with a light towing limit, and the J endorsement allows heavier towing.
Restriction codes limit a license, while endorsements add a privilege and need extra tests.
Renewing on time is your responsibility, and changes of address or name must be reported within thirty days.
Restricted licenses are special exceptions for hardship, school travel or a half-served suspension.
A Nevada ID card needs age ten and lasts eight years, unless limited-term documents end it sooner.
Getting an ID card surrenders your driving privilege, and citations still count against you.
Fees are set by state law, and drivers sixty-five and older pay less.
